reuse.why: The change reuses getScheduledAmount, but duplicates getApproxNumberThreshold and retains caller-side decisions already handled by the amount helper.

duplication.why: Three consumers retain missing/number/range dispatch, and the shared helper copies the existing approximate-tolerance calculation.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, and API serialization remains in the existing schedule model.

scope.why: The edits focus on expected schedule amounts, their consumers, and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Optional operator propagation and retained caller-side dispatch leave ownership of the amount policy split across consumers.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts reimplements shared/rules.ts:getApproxNumberThreshold; schedules/app.ts:updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, plus computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, bypass getScheduledAmount for missing and numeric values.

disguised_duplication.where: updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions delegate only the range branch while retaining duplicated missing/number/range selection around the shared helper.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains optional op and an isapprox branch; three consumers retain numeric bypasses, while schedule-template.ts and existing consumers omit the operator needed to select the expanded policy.
